label: rem:markov-lambda-knot-operations
title: Knot operations, Markov chain, and the partition $\lambda$
html:
Remark. Knot operations, Markov chain, and the partition \lambda

Superseded. The scalar substrate density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower).

The Markov chain, knot-theoretic operations, and the partition \lambda are linked by explicit structural statements that govern traffic between \lambda-preserving and \lambda-changing moves.

1. \lambda-block decomposition. Semisimplicity decomposes H_n(R, q) into endomorphism algebras over V_\lambda. The amplitude matrix splits into a direct sum over \lambda. Each \lambda acts as a closed sector. Hecke-generator amplitudes never mix irreps.

2. \lambda-preserving and \lambda-changing operations. Knot operations separate sharply. Braid relations, the Hecke quadratic, and Markov I moves fix \lambda. Only the Markov II stabilization move changes \lambda, and it does so exclusively by adding a single box along a Young-graph edge.

Stabilization acts as a transition on the coarser partition chain, transitioning at a rate proportional to the q-Plancherel measure.

3. Jones polynomial as Plancherel sum. The Jones polynomial factorizes as a sum over \lambda of Ocneanu-weighted q-characters. This establishes an explicit classical/quantum split. The normalized weights form a classical probability measure on \lambda, while the character computes a quantum-amplitude sum over \mathrm{SYT}(\lambda). The partition \lambda serves as the classical label, and the SYT paths represent the quantum trajectories.
